name: Canberra Times cryptic crossword, Thursday 18 December 1975

clue.text: Fashions go through various phases

indicators.note: to go through various forms is to change shape repeatedly, so the next word's letters are rearranged

blocks.note: taken as written, then rearranged

explanation.surface: Fashion trends cycle through one phase after another.
explanation.definitionFit: To fashion something is to mould or form it, so the verb is a synonym in the third person.

clue.text: Verbal approval of a brace of cooked hare!

indicators.note: cooking transforms an ingredient, so the animal's letters are reworked
a brace is a pair of game birds or animals, so the rearranged word is needed twice over

blocks.note: the animal's letters rearranged
the same rearrangement once more, making the pair

explanation.surface: A cook is praised for serving up a pair of hares.
explanation.walkthrough: A brace is the sporting word for two head of game, which tells you to make the rearranged word twice.
explanation.definitionFit: The doubled cry is the traditional spoken shout of agreement used in Parliament and at public meetings.

clue.text: He couldn't complain of growing pains,

definitions.text: He couldn't complain of growing pains

blocks.clueFragment: He couldn't complain of growing pains
blocks.note: surface: someone too healthy to suffer the aches of adolescence
setter's reading: the boy in question never grew up at all, so never had them

explanation.surface: A youngster who never suffered the aches of adolescence.
explanation.definitionFit: J. M. Barrie's hero is the boy who refused to grow up, so he could never have adolescent aches.

clue.text: It's illuminating up to a point

definitions.text: It's illuminating up to a point

blocks.clueFragment: It's illuminating up to a point
blocks.note: surface: something only partly enlightening
setter's reading: a lamp that throws light onto a single spot

explanation.surface: Something that is informative, though only to a limited extent.
explanation.definitionFit: A stage lamp throws a narrow beam that lights one small area, literally lighting a point.

clue.text: A . visionary is not dependent on this

definitions.text: visionary is not dependent on this

blocks.note: surface: a dreamer or seer of the future
setter's reading: a seer's visions come without the use of the eyes

explanation.surface: A prophet's insight needs no ordinary means of seeing.
explanation.walkthrough: The stray full stop is a blemish from the newspaper scan.
explanation.definitionFit: Ordinary physical sight is the faculty a mystic's inner visions do without.

clue.text: Their recipients are not single-minded

blocks.note: surface: people who are distracted or divided in purpose
setter's reading: people who have no wish to stay single

explanation.surface: Some people who are given something are easily distracted.
explanation.definitionFit: Those receiving these tokens have agreed to marry, so they plainly intend not to remain unmarried.

clue.text: In the main, insular

definitions.note: a phrase meaning surrounded by ocean

blocks.note: first meaning: out in the open ocean, the main being an old word for the sea
second meaning: forming an island

explanation.surface: Someone who is, by and large, narrow-minded.
explanation.walkthrough: The main is an old poetic word for the open sea.
explanation.definitionFit: Girt means encircled, so a place ringed by ocean is an island, the literal sense of insular.

clue.text: One doesn't need a licence to drive it

definitions.text: One doesn't need a licence to drive it

blocks.clueFragment: One doesn't need a licence to drive it
blocks.note: surface: a vehicle anyone may take on the road
setter's reading: drive as a long shot off the tee

explanation.surface: A vehicle you can take on the road without a permit.
explanation.definitionFit: Players strike this small dimpled sphere off the tee with a driver, which needs no permit.

clue.text: But it does not necessarily have a floating population

definitions.text: But it does not necessarily have a floating population

blocks.note: surface: residents who come and go
setter's reading: the word ends in a vessel, which would carry people afloat, yet this place need not

explanation.surface: A settlement whose residents mostly stay put.
explanation.walkthrough: The joke is that the word ends in SHIP, a craft whose population really floats.
explanation.definitionFit: A township is a small town or administrative district, a settled community on land.

clue.text: But it 'is generally rendered in full

blocks.note: setter's reading: despite its name suggesting a portion only
surface: usually performed complete; also sung by a full choir

explanation.surface: Something usually performed or translated without cuts.
explanation.walkthrough: The joke is that the name begins with PART, yet the piece is sung in full; the apostrophe is a scan blemish.
explanation.definitionFit: A part-song is a choral piece for several voices, usually unaccompanied, so it is sung whole by a group.

clue.text: Venerate all who reform

indicators.note: to reform is to shape anew, so the preceding words are rearranged

blocks.note: taken as written, then rearranged

explanation.surface: Respect anyone who turns over a new leaf.
explanation.definitionFit: To hallow is to honour as holy, a close synonym of venerating something.

clue.text: Limping cricketer?

blocks.note: first meaning: hobbling with one limb shorter than the other
second meaning: a fielder placed close in on the leg side

explanation.surface: A cricket player hobbling after an injury.
explanation.walkthrough: Short leg is a cricket fielding position close to the batsman on the leg side, and the fielder there is called by its name.
explanation.definitionFit: A person with one shortened limb limps, and the fielder stationed at that close position shares the name.

clue.text: Cloud of saintly associations

definitions.note: an adjectival phrase for a noun: the halo associated with saints

blocks.note: first meaning: a dark rain cloud
second meaning: the bright disc painted round a holy head

explanation.surface: A cloud linked in some way with holy people.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names a grey rain-bearing cloud and also the halo of light shown around saints in paintings.

clue.text: All agreed there is no occasion for this

definitions.text: All agreed there is no occasion for this

blocks.note: surface: everyone consented to something
setter's reading: when everyone agrees, there is nothing to dispute

explanation.surface: A group unanimously decides that some event will not be held.
explanation.definitionFit: A dispute or quarrel only arises when people disagree, so unanimity leaves no cause for one.

clue.text: He certainly didn't take a poor view of himself

definitions.text: He certainly didn't take a poor view of himself

blocks.clueFragment: didn't take a poor view of himself
blocks.note: surface: a man with a high opinion of himself
setter's reading: literally gazing at his own reflection

explanation.surface: A conceited man who thought well of himself.
explanation.definitionFit: In Greek myth the youth fell in love with his own reflection in a pool, the original self-admirer.

clue.text: Architectural bird

blocks.note: first meaning: Sir Christopher, designer of St Paul's Cathedral in London
second meaning: a tiny brown songbird

explanation.surface: A bird that builds elaborate structures.
explanation.walkthrough: The adjective stands for the most famous English architect, read as a name.
explanation.definitionFit: The surname belongs to the great seventeenth-century English architect and also names a small songbird.

clue.text: They have scant regard for their betters

definitions.text: They have scant regard for their betters

blocks.note: surface: people who disrespect their superiors
setter's reading: people who place bets, whom these characters fail to pay

explanation.surface: Insolent people who show no respect for their social superiors.
explanation.definitionFit: To welsh is to fail to pay a gambling debt, so these cheats ignore the punters owed money.

clue.text: Needing a change? Try part of Switzerland

indicators.note: the first word needs alteration, so its letters with the article are rearranged

blocks.note: taken as written, then rearranged

explanation.surface: A travel agent suggests a Swiss holiday to someone who needs a break.
explanation.walkthrough: The article does double duty: it is fodder and also part of the phrase signalling change.
explanation.definitionFit: The Engadine is the high valley of the Inn in eastern Switzerland, home of St Moritz.

clue.text: Thin way for the launch

definitions.note: an adjective for a noun: a slip is a slim young person

blocks.note: first meaning: as in a slender young person
second meaning: the sloping ramp down which a new vessel slides into the water

explanation.surface: A narrow route used for a launch event.
explanation.definitionFit: A slip is both a slender person and the inclined ramp, or slipway, from which ships are launched.

clue.text: "To the last — of recorded time" (Mac beth)

definitions.text: "To the last — of recorded time" (Mac beth)

blocks.note: the quotation with one word missing
the source: the 'Tomorrow and tomorrow' speech

explanation.walkthrough: Fill the gap: Macbeth says that tomorrow creeps on to the last syllable of recorded time.
explanation.definitionFit: The missing word is the unit of speech that completes Shakespeare's famous line in the tragedy.

clue.text: Conspiracy to fascinate

blocks.note: first meaning: a secret plot
second meaning: to arouse curiosity

explanation.surface: A plot designed to captivate someone.
explanation.definitionFit: The noun means a secret scheme, and the verb means to arouse keen interest or curiosity.

clue.text: Fish with something in common with the bee? .

definitions.text: Fish with something in common with the bee?

blocks.note: the kind of creature wanted: a flat sea fish

blocks.clueFragment: something in common with the bee?
blocks.note: setter's reading: the venomous weapon a bee carries, which this fish has on its tail

explanation.surface: A sea creature that shares a feature with a bee.
explanation.walkthrough: The name joins the bee's weapon to the family of flat fish it belongs to. The trailing full stop is a scan blemish.
explanation.definitionFit: This flat sea creature is a type of ray with a venomous barbed spine on its tail.

clue.text: Dismissal for wining with Falstaff?

blocks.note: first meaning: firing from a job
second meaning: drinking sack, the sherry-like wine Falstaff loves in Henry IV

explanation.surface: An employee is fired for drinking on the job with Shakespeare's fat knight.
explanation.walkthrough: Sack was an old fortified white wine from Spain, Falstaff's favourite drink.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means being fired, and whimsically means drinking sack, as Shakespeare's knight constantly did.

clue.text: Something a runaway makes himself

blocks.note: surface: an object a fugitive builds
setter's reading: the idiom to make oneself absent or hard to find

explanation.surface: A fugitive fashions something by his own hand.
explanation.definitionFit: To make yourself scarce is the idiom for leaving or keeping out of the way, as anyone fleeing does.

clue.text: It is, in a word, bad in - age

definitions.text: It is, in a word, bad in - age

blocks.note: surface: something poor in old times
setter's reading: join the pieces into one word, badinage, meaning teasing talk

explanation.surface: Something said to be bad in its time.
explanation.walkthrough: Run the three pieces together to get badinage, playful banter; the dash is a scan blemish.
explanation.definitionFit: Badinage is light teasing banter, which is exactly what good-humoured mockery or ridicule amounts to.

clue.text: Methuselah" favourite -drink?

blocks.note: surface: the Bible's longest-lived man, 969 years
setter's reading: the drink of life that would explain such a lifespan

explanation.surface: What the oldest man in the Bible liked to drink.
explanation.walkthrough: The stray marks after Methuselah and before drink are scan blemishes for an apostrophe-s and a space.
explanation.definitionFit: The fabled elixir of life was believed to grant immortality or very long life, fitting the patriarch.

clue.text: They include courses for horses

blocks.note: surface: racecourses
setter's reading: courses of a meal, held in a feed bag

explanation.surface: Venues that include tracks for racing horses.
explanation.definitionFit: These feeding bags strapped over a horse's muzzle hold its meal, so they contain its food courses.

clue.text: Snug nest arranged for potential killers

indicators.note: to arrange is to put in a new order, so the two preceding words are reordered

blocks.note: taken as written, then rearranged

explanation.surface: A cosy home is set up for future murderers.
explanation.walkthrough: The scan reads rest, but only nest gives the second N the answer needs.
explanation.definitionFit: Sten guns are British submachine guns of the Second World War, weapons capable of killing.

clue.text: Tantrums in the theatre

definitions.note: a phrase standing for theatrical divisions

blocks.note: first meaning: public displays of temper
second meaning: subdivisions of a play's acts

explanation.surface: Actors throwing fits backstage.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means public displays of anger and also the subdivisions of an act in drama.
